source: NCERT Class XII, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch. 4 (Human Development).

sections.heading: 1. Concept of Human Development
points: **Human development** = enlarging people's **choices, freedoms and well-being** — not just economic growth.
The concept was developed by **Mahbub ul Haq** and **Amartya Sen**.
The **UNDP Human Development Report** (from 1990) measures it.

sections.heading: 2. The Four Pillars
points: **Equity** — equal access to opportunities for all (regardless of gender, race, income).
**Sustainability** — meeting present needs without harming future generations.
**Productivity** — human labour productivity, built by investing in people.
**Empowerment** — the power to make choices and influence one's life (especially of the marginalised).

sections.heading: 3. Measuring Human Development — HDI
points: The **Human Development Index (HDI)** combines three dimensions:

sub: **A long and healthy life** — measured by **life expectancy**.
**Knowledge** — measured by education (mean and expected years of schooling).
**A decent standard of living** — measured by **per capita income (GNI)**.

points: HDI ranges from 0 to 1; countries grouped into **very high, high, medium, low** human development.

sections.heading: 4. Approaches and Other Indices
points: Approaches to human development: **income, welfare, basic needs, and capability (Sen)** approaches.
Other indices: **Gender Development Index (GDI), Gender Inequality Index (GII), Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), Human Poverty Index**.
Human development shifts focus from wealth to **people and their capabilities**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Human development concept: Mahbub ul Haq + Amartya Sen; UNDP HDR (1990).
Four pillars: equity, sustainability, productivity, empowerment.
HDI = health (life expectancy) + education + income (per capita GNI).
Approaches: income, welfare, basic needs, capability (Sen).
Other indices: GDI, GII, MPI.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **HDI has three dimensions: health, education, income** (published by UNDP).
The four pillars = **equity, sustainability, productivity, empowerment**.
The **capability approach** is associated with **Amartya Sen**.
Human development is about **enlarging choices**, not just income growth.
